terms.definition: A serve that scores directly because the other team can't return it.
terms.example: She closed the set with an ace down the line.

terms.definition: A thin rod on each side of the net that marks the side limit for crossing. A ball that touches it is out.
terms.example: The swing was hard but clipped the antenna, so the point went the other way.

terms.definition: Any hit, other than a serve or block, that sends the ball toward the other team. Usually the third touch.
terms.example: After a perfect pass, the attack went to the outside hitter.

terms.definition: The line 3 m from the centre line that separates the front zone from the back zone.
terms.example: Back-row hitters must jump from behind the attack line.

terms.definition: Zones 5, 6 and 1. Back-row players may not block, or attack a ball fully above the net from in front of the attack line.
terms.example: The setter is in the back row for half of the rotations.

terms.definition: An attack by a back-row player who takes off from behind the attack line.
terms.example: Their outside hitter swung a back-row attack from zone 6.

terms.definition: A front-row player's attempt to stop an attack by reaching above the net. It doesn't count as a team touch.
terms.example: Two blockers closed the seam and the attack came straight back.

terms.definition: Everyday name for the forearm pass.
terms.example: Bump it high to the setter.

terms.definition: The line under the net that splits the court into two halves.
terms.example: Her foot crossed the centre line completely, so it was a fault.

terms.definition: Teammates crouching around an attacking hitter, ready to play a ball blocked back.
terms.example: Good cover kept the rally alive after the block.

terms.definition: The part of the net's vertical plane between the antennae that the ball must pass through.
terms.example: The overpass went outside the crossing space, so it was out.

terms.definition: A back-row substitute (DS) brought in for passing and defence.
terms.example: The coach subbed in a defensive specialist for the middle's back-row turn.

terms.definition: Passing a hard-driven attack, usually with the forearms.
terms.example: The libero dug the spike right to the setter.

terms.definition: One player touching the ball twice in a row. Allowed only on a block or in one action on the team's first touch.
terms.example: The setter's hands weren't even, so the ref called a double contact.

terms.definition: An attack hit from a standing position or low jump, usually when the set is off.
terms.example: The set was too far off the net, so he hit a down ball.

terms.definition: The back boundary of the court. The server stands behind it.
terms.example: The serve landed right on the end line, so it was in.

terms.definition: A rules violation. It ends the rally and gives the other team the point.
terms.example: Four touches is a fault even if the last one goes over.

terms.definition: A system with one setter who sets in all six rotations and five hitters.
terms.example: In our 5-1 the setter starts in zone 1 in rotation 1.

terms.definition: A serve hit with no spin, so it moves unpredictably in the air.
terms.example: Her float serve dropped just as the passer moved.

terms.definition: Touching the court or end line before hitting the serve.
terms.example: He stepped on the end line as he served, so it was a foot fault.

terms.definition: An easy ball sent over without an attack. The call tells teammates to get into passing spots.
terms.example: "Free ball!" The middle dropped off the net to pass.

terms.definition: Zones 4, 3 and 2, closest to the net. Only front-row players may block.
terms.example: The setter is in the front row in rotations 4, 5 and 6.

terms.definition: A serve hit at the top of a run-up and jump for extra power.
terms.example: His jump serve was too fast to pass cleanly.

terms.definition: An attack that scores directly.
terms.example: She had twelve kills in the first set.

terms.definition: A serve that touches the net and still crosses into the other court. Legal under FIVB rules.
terms.example: The let serve trickled over and dropped for an ace.

terms.definition: A back-row specialist in a contrasting jersey. Plays only in zones 5, 6 and 1, and may not block or attempt to block.
terms.example: The libero came in for the middle blocker in zone 6.

terms.definition: A ball that is held, caught or thrown instead of hit cleanly. Also called a catch.
terms.example: The ref called a lift on the one-handed save.

terms.definition: An official who uses a flag to signal whether a ball is in or out.
terms.example: The line judge flagged the serve out.

terms.definition: A front-row player (MB) who blocks across the net and hits quick sets from zone 3.
terms.example: The middle blocker read the setter and closed the block.

terms.definition: Touching the net between the antennae while playing the ball.
terms.example: He brushed the tape on the way down, so it was a net fault.

terms.definition: The hitter (OPP) who plays across from the setter in the rotation and attacks from right front.
terms.example: The opposite hit a big swing from zone 2.

terms.definition: A hitter (OH) who attacks from left front and also passes in serve receive.
terms.example: The set went high to the outside hitter in zone 4.

terms.definition: A positional fault: a receiving player out of rotation order when the ball is served.
terms.example: Zone 4 was standing behind zone 5 at the serve, so the ref called an overlap.

terms.definition: A first or second touch that goes over the net by accident.
terms.example: The pass was an overpass and their middle put it away.

terms.definition: The first touch, usually a forearm pass, sending the ball to the setter.
terms.example: A good pass lets the setter run any play.

terms.definition: A back-row attack from the middle of the court, behind the attack line.
terms.example: The setter dished a pipe to the outside in zone 6.

terms.definition: The flat surface made by joining your hands and locking your forearms to pass.
terms.example: Keep your platform angled at the setter.

terms.definition: A fast, low set to a middle blocker who is already jumping.
terms.example: The quick set beat the block before it formed.

terms.definition: A scoring system where every rally ends in a point, no matter who served.
terms.example: Under rally scoring, a missed serve gives the other team a point.

terms.definition: The first referee runs the match from a raised stand; the second referee works on the floor on the other side.
terms.example: The first referee whistled for the serve.

terms.definition: A soft attack with topspin, hit over the block into open space.
terms.example: She saw the deep defence and used a roll shot.

terms.definition: Moving one zone clockwise after winning the serve back. Also the name for each of the six lineups.
terms.example: We're in rotation 1, so the setter is serving.

terms.definition: The hit that starts each rally, made by the player in zone 1 from behind the end line.
terms.example: You have 8 seconds after the whistle to serve.

terms.definition: The formation and passing a team uses when the other team is serving.
terms.example: Three passers split the court in serve receive.

terms.definition: The 9 m wide area behind the end line where the server stands.
terms.example: Serve from anywhere in the service zone.

terms.definition: One game within a match. Regular sets go to 25 and the deciding set to 15, both won by 2.
terms.example: They won the first set 25–22.

terms.definition: An overhead fingertip touch that places the ball for a hitter, usually the second touch.
terms.example: The set was perfect, right at the antenna.

terms.definition: The player (S) who takes the second touch and decides who attacks.
terms.example: The setter faked to the middle and set the outside.

terms.definition: A badly mis-hit pass that goes far from the target.
terms.example: The serve hit his wrist and he shanked it into the stands.

terms.definition: Winning a rally while the other team is serving. You score, win the serve and rotate.
terms.example: We sided out and rotated our outside hitter back to serve.

terms.definition: A system with two setters who each set from the back row, so there are always three front-row hitters.
terms.example: In a 6-2, the setter in the front row becomes a hitter.

terms.definition: A hard, downward attack hit at the top of a jump.
terms.example: She spiked it cross-court for the kill.

terms.definition: A block that sends the ball straight down onto the attacker's side for a point.
terms.example: The middle stuff-blocked the quick set.

terms.definition: Replacing one player with another. FIVB allows six per team per set; libero replacements don't count.
terms.example: The coach used a substitution to bring in a server.

terms.definition: A 30-second break a team can call. FIVB allows two per team per set.
terms.example: Down 3 points, the coach called a timeout.

terms.definition: A soft fingertip touch that drops the ball over or around the block.
terms.example: She tipped it into the open middle of the court.

terms.definition: A serve with forward spin that dives down quickly.
terms.example: The topspin serve dropped right inside the end line.

terms.definition: Switching from defence to attack after your team digs or blocks the ball.
terms.example: After the dig, the middle transitioned off the net to hit.

terms.definition: One of six areas on each half. Front row 4, 3, 2 and back row 5, 6, 1, with the net at the top.
terms.example: The server stands in zone 1.
